requirement:
The coverage overview identifies itself as documented coverage gaps and
explains that `habeas status` and `habeas author` check the annotations and
reviews, while `habeas coverage-check` enforces measured coverage.
It presents no coverage-check pass/fail verdict.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps` has no structural obligations. It has no implementation roots, and none are needed. Each clause describes what the coverage overview shows:
- "identifies itself as documented coverage gaps"
- "explains that `habeas status` and `habeas author` check the annotations and reviews, while `habeas coverage-check` enforces measured coverage"
- "presents no coverage-check pass/fail verdict"

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface. Any way of producing the overview with the same content satisfies it. A hand-written page, a generated page and a template all conform. So none of the clauses is a structural obligation.

behavioral: Obligations in `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps`: (1) the overview identifies itself as documented coverage gaps; (2) it explains that `habeas status` and `habeas author` check annotations and reviews, while `habeas coverage-check` enforces measured coverage; (3) it presents no coverage-check pass/fail verdict.

(1) and (2) are covered by `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts]`. It asserts the overview starts with `# Documented coverage gaps`. It also asserts the overview contains both explanatory sentences, one for `habeas status` and `habeas author` and one for `habeas coverage-check`. The chapter name "Documented coverage gaps" is asserted there too.

(3) is covered by three tests:
- `book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts` asserts that the overview omits "CI would", "Line coverage:" and "0 unresolved gaps". It also asserts the overview is identical whether or not saved measurements exist, including invalid or corrupt ones.
- `documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups` asserts the HTML lacks "CI would", "gap-verdict", "gap-percentage", "instrumented lines covered" and "data-status=".
- `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` renders the overview while `report(root).passed` is false and then true. It does the same with the profile data removed, and with reviews set to Missing, true, false and FIXME. It asserts the rendered book has no "CI would" text. It also asserts the render is identical before and after the CLI check goes from pass to fail, so no verdict follows measurement state.

The requirement does not fix any verdict wording. The tests rule out the verdict markers and measurement-dependent output that the requirement would forbid. I found no gap.
